title: Behind the Counter
tagline: When a team keeps doing a chore by hand, I build them a tool for it.
what: Work comes to me from the sales team, customer service, the warehouse, accounting and purchasing: taking orders, shipping them, counting stock and checking the bills.
does: Build the screen reps take orders and quotes on, with shipping prices up front
Teach the support bot to answer "where's my order" on its own
Clean customer data: addresses, home or business flags, duplicate records
Run the shipping station: labels, packing slips, tracking, delivery notices
Handle customs, duties and export paperwork for overseas orders
Test and reprogram hardware on a bench tool the warehouse uses
Build the warehouse's count and repair logs, and the checks that make month-end tie out
Check sales tax, carrier bills and payments so mistakes surface before anyone pays

solved.problem: Our shipping carrier shut down the tool we used to quote and print labels.
solved.did: Moved quoting and labels over, and built a shipping station so we print our own carrier labels.
solved.ended: Shipping works from it every day.

solved.problem: Shipping bills were too long to check by eye, and double charges slipped through.
solved.did: Built a check that matches every shipping charge to a real shipment and flags anything billed twice.
solved.ended: Double charges surface on their own now, and nearly every line matches without anyone checking by hand.

solved.problem: Repairs and part-outs lived in a spreadsheet nobody trusted.
solved.did: Replaced it with a log the warehouse fills in as they take units apart, which builds the write-off list by itself.
solved.ended: The old sheet was retired and the log is the record.

solved.problem: Customer addresses carried the wrong home or business type, so shipping rates came out wrong.
solved.did: Built an address checker for customer service, with a one-page guide, then fixed the old records in bulk.
solved.ended: Customer service uses it, and rates come out right.

worksWith: Sales, customer service, shipping, the warehouse, accounting, finance, purchasing, leadership, a developer, the carriers.
story: A rep can pick a customer, build an order, see real shipping prices and send a quote from one screen. I built it with customer service, then handed it over to reps and a warehouse tech.
Before it, quoting meant jumping between systems to find the customer, the products and the shipping price.

I got the first version running end to end on a safe copy, then sat with customer service and worked through their notes. Card payments, discounts and approvals followed, so a rep could give a customer a break with accounting in the loop.
I watched it run on real orders before the handover. Store credit, thirty-day quotes and confirmation emails followed.
Underneath it, I lined up what counts as a customer, a dealer and a sale. The price the rep sees matches what gets billed.
credit: The job, plus the tools I built for it
